subject: Clarify: 'end of day' vs timestamp cutoff for SOC 2 Type II (Dec snapshot)
messages:
From: Jake Morrison <jake@brightpathaudit.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II - Dec 31 snapshot: inclusive end point?

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as we prepare the SOC 2 Type II cover memo for Acme: the client is asking whether Redwood's December 2027 "snapshot" is interpreted as inclusive through 2027-12-31 23:59:59 local time (the client operates US/Eastern) or whether your point-in-time evidence is taken strictly at the timestamp 2027-12-31T00:00:00Z (i.e., an instant at midnight UTC).

Practically this matters for log extracts and the sample we plan to request; if you consider "end of day" inclusive we will pull up to 23:59:59 local and request the final syslog roll; if it's an instant we will only request the precise timestamped record.

Can you confirm Redwood's interpretation and whether you provide a bridge letter for partial-day transitions (we've seen clients want that when local timezone vs UTC rounding affects counts)? I've attached the draft cover PDF and an example log extract we might ask for.

Thanks,
Jake

--
Jake Morrison

jake@brightpathaudit.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments referenced: SOC2-TypeII-2027-cover.pdf (draft), syslogs-sample-20271231.csv (example)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morrison <jake@brightpathaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II - Dec 31 snapshot: inclusive end point?

Hi Jake — thanks for the note and for flagging what Acme needs. Short answer: our standard practice for the Type II report is to treat a monthly snapshot as inclusive through the last second of the calendar day in the customer's local timezone unless otherwise specified. In other words, December 31, 2027 would be inclusive through 2027-12-31 23:59:59 in the customer's local time (US/Eastern for Acme).

A few clarifications so the audit team can draft the evidence request properly:
- Our system stores events in UTC; when we produce a point-in-time snapshot we translate to the customer's timezone for inclusivity semantics (we include all events with UTC timestamps that map to the local date ending at 23:59:59).
- For audit reproducibility we can also provide the raw UTC cutoff timestamp we used, plus a mapping file showing the timezone conversion we applied (helps avoid ambiguity when daylight savings or leap seconds are involved).
- We can provide a bridge letter confirming the translation rule and that the snapshot includes the full local calendar day; if Acme needs a separate signed bridge letter we can produce it with Redwoods' compliance signature.

I'll loop in Marissa and Neha for any additional evidence or specific artifact names you prefer (log manifest, S3 object keys, manifest checksum, etc.). If that works, please confirm the exact evidence window you want us to export (e.g., 2027-12-01T00:00:00 local -> 2027-12-31T23:59:59 local) and whether you need the UTC cutoff value included in the deliverable.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II - Dec 31 snapshot: inclusive end point?

Thanks Karthik — confirming from the evidence side: we can produce the following artifacts for Acme and BrightPath to avoid any ambiguity:

1) A log manifest CSV listing S3 object keys and start/end UTC timestamps for each object covering 2027-12-31 local day; includes file sizes and SHA256 checksums.
2) A small sample export (syslogs-sample-20271231.csv) with the last 10 events of the day (UTC timestamps included) so you can validate inclusivity.
3) A one-page bridge letter stating: "Redwood Inference interprets a calendar-day snapshot as inclusive through 23:59:59 in the customer's local timezone; provided UTC cutoff is X" — we will populate X with the UTC timestamp equivalent once you confirm which local timezone to apply.
4) Optional: we can also include a tiny script and a mapping file that shows how UTC timestamps were bucketed to local dates (handy for your sample checks).

Jake — if Acme confirms US/Eastern we will set the UTC cutoff to 2028-01-01T04:59:59Z (accounting for EST/EDT depending on the date). Please confirm whether you need the whole December window or just the single-day snapshot at month-end.

Neha, assigning to you to prepare the bridge letter draft and the manifest export once Jake confirms the window.

Marissa
Senior Manager, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

- The manifest CSV with S3 keys and UTC start/end timestamps for the objects covering 2027-12-31 (so we can validate full-day coverage).

- The bridge letter draft; we'll route it to Acme legal for signature concurrently with our report.
